p: South Woodham Ferrers is a bit of an oddity in Essex: a town largely built from the 1970s onwards, planned by Essex County Council around a market square designed to look like an old Essex town, with weatherboarding and clay tiles. It works surprisingly well, and the town centre has shops, cafés and the essentials you'll want for a day out.

For extra things to do, Marsh Farm Country Park on the edge of town is a great add-on, with walks out towards the River Crouch, open grassland and big skies. The estuary itself is a haven for wading birds, especially in winter, so binoculars are worth packing. Hanningfield Reservoir, a few miles inland, has woodland trails and a visitor centre run by Essex Wildlife Trust.

The town has a station on the Crouch Valley line, with trains towards Wickford and on to London, while Chelmsford is a short drive for bigger shops and leisure. As with any smaller animal attraction, opening patterns can change, so look up the latest details before you set off.
